intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honor all of them. Today's roll was seed 3417333311. Here is each roll and what came of it, as filed with the Harbour Board.

rolls.became: In fog a lighthouse is useless: the beam can't reach anybody. But the smell of steamed dumplings carries for miles in wet air, so an old Harbour Board bylaw says a station in fog shall make itself known by any means. Skerry Light's means are dumplings. Every boat that follows its nose in gets fed.

A lighthouse has no hands, but it does have clockwork: the gears that turn the lamp. Skerry Light hooked them to a pleating wheel. One turn, one pleat. Gearing it up, and hiring gulls to help, is most of the shop.

A lighthouse has no counters, only up. So the bamboo steamers go on a tray below the winch, one on top of another. The basket swings; you tap to drop it. Miss and it goes to the gulls. Lean too far and the whole stack goes over.

The lighthouse trembles, and the trembling shakes the swing and the stack. Missed boats and toppled stacks make it worse; perfect drops, chamomile, a cardigan from the Welfare Committee and the shipping forecast on the radio calm it down. Watch its eyebrows.
The season's quota, 720 dumplings, is the meter at the top. A lighthouse has exactly one job, and in fog season this is it.

Regulation 18: every dumpling shall have exactly eighteen pleats. That's the ring of eighteen ticks next to the basket. Drop the basket while a dumpling is still on the wheel and it goes off at eleven or seventeen pleats and is rejected.

Boats wait in the fog as contract slips: how many dumplings, how many chits. Pick one and it comes alongside; stack enough dumplings before it sails and the winch lowers the stack onto its deck. Prawn and soup permits bring better-paying orders. Soup wants a straight stack.

A few minutes in, the Board puts an automatic light at Eastpoint and tells it to learn from you. It does. Everything you buy, it buys forty seconds later, slightly wrong (a cardigam, a bamboo dowl). Its little stack copies yours three seconds late, topples and all. And any boat you leave waiting too long, Eastpoint feeds.
720 dumplings is the whole season, prices run to a couple of hundred chits, and a big order is a few dozen dumplings. Eighteen pleats each, though, so the pleat count isn't small.
About half an hour: one fog season, from the first basket to Form 99.

rolls.value: hand it all over to someone else
rolls.became: When the quota is met, Form 99 arrives: transfer of catering duties to Eastpoint. You stack the whole kitchen into crates (the clockwork, the baskets, the cardigan, the gulls) for Eastpoint's tender.

rolls.value: it gets undone, and that's fine
rolls.became: Eastpoint copied everything, one tooth short. Its first dumpling comes undone in the steamer at seventeen pleats. The skipper eats it anyway: tastes the same. Then the Board finally answers Form 18-B (the silly one-off that sat on the shelf saying 'pending' all game): Regulation 18 is struck. Nobody else was counting. The lighthouse stops trembling and turns its lamp back on.

Everything is printed in flat inks that overprint and sit slightly out of register, on cream paper, with halftone dots for the sky and the sea. The gull and the boats started as game-icons.net shapes and were reprinted as two misregistered plates.
Purple ink, teal, aqua, peach and coral on cream: coral for the lighthouse stripes and the steamers, teal for the sea and the paperwork, aqua for glass and for Eastpoint, which is very clean.

A quiet kalimba tune in D harmonic minor over a soft bass. When Eastpoint arrives, a second kalimba starts copying the melody a bar late, from the other side. Every sound effect is on the same scale, and Eastpoint's copy of your purchase jingle is slightly out of tune. At the very end the tune turns to D major.

Forms. Form 7 (incident), Form 22 (prawns), Form 31 (structural support, edible-adjacent), Form 41 (automatic release of baskets, supervised; nobody is supervising), Form 18-B (pending; please do not resubmit).

outro: Regulation 18 was very clear. It just turned out nobody else was reading it.
